hero.subtitle: Goliath Dispatch is the system of record for US transportation dispatch companies: carrier onboarding and compliance, load dispatch, tracking, permits and escorts, and settlements — bilingual from the first screen.

item1.title: One system, not five spreadsheets
item1.body: Dispatch, carrier compliance, documents, invoicing and tracking live in one place instead of a spreadsheet, a shared drive and a phone full of texts.

item2.title: Compliance gates that actually block a bad dispatch
item2.body: FMCSA authority, COI-to-VIN matches, driver credentials and equipment photos are checked automatically before a load can be assigned — not caught after the fact.

item3.title: Financials that don't get rewritten
item3.body: Every settlement is computed in integer cents and saved as a permanent snapshot. When a fee percentage changes next quarter, last month's math doesn't change with it.

item4.title: Bilingual from the ground up
item4.body: English and Spanish are both first-class, not a translated afterthought — because your dispatchers, carriers and drivers already work in both.

oversizeBand.title: Heavy-haul and oversize, without the guesswork
oversizeBand.body: Permit and escort requirements are evaluated against your load's dimensions, weight and route before it's dispatched, using each state's baseline rules. It's operational guidance your team can plan around — not a substitute for the permit itself.

step1.title: Carrier onboards
step1.body: Legal name, DOT/MC, Certificate of Insurance, W-9 and, if factoring applies, a Notice of Assignment — submitted once.

step2.title: Equipment verified
step2.body: VIN matched to the COI, four photos minimum, registration and inspection current before any assignment.

step3.title: Load dispatched
step3.body: Compliance gates run automatically. A load with an expired document or an unconfirmed escort cannot move.

step4.title: Tracked
step4.body: The carrier and the customer both see live status. The customer gets a secure link — not another login to manage.

step5.title: Settled
step5.body: Dispatch fee, reimbursables and deductions computed the same way every time, recorded as an immutable snapshot.

hero.title: Heavy haul & oversize
hero.subtitle: Oversize and overweight freight isn't a special mode — it's freight with a permit requirement, an escort requirement, or both. Here's how Goliath Dispatch evaluates it, and where that evaluation stops.

legalLimits.title: Federal legal-limit baseline
legalLimits.body: Without a permit, the baseline most states apply is 8'6" wide, 13'6" tall, and 80,000 lb gross weight on a standard five-axle configuration, with trailer length commonly capped around 53'. Every state sets its own permit thresholds at or above that baseline, and several set tighter limits on specific roads, bridges or through certain cities.

permitTriggers.title: What triggers a permit
permitTriggers.body: Exceeding a state's legal width, height, length or weight limit — even by a few inches or a few hundred pounds — requires a permit for that state. Some states also require a permit for a load within legal dimensions if its axle weight distribution exceeds the bridge formula for that route.

escortTriggers.title: What triggers an escort
escortTriggers.body: Most states require a pilot car once width passes a state-specific threshold, commonly between 12' and 14'. Height that risks overhead obstructions, and length beyond roughly 100'–110' combined, typically add a rear or front escort requirement. Several states require a police escort above certain dimensions or on specific designated routes.

routeSurveys.title: When a route survey is required
routeSurveys.body: Height close to a bridge or wire clearance, or a route through a city with load-specific detours, calls for a physical route survey before the trip — not just a routing calculation. Goliath Dispatch flags when your load's height or width crosses the threshold where a survey is standard practice; performing the survey itself is a service your team or your escort provider carries out.

stateVariation.title: Why "the rule" isn't one rule
stateVariation.body: Permit thresholds, escort thresholds, travel curfews and required equipment — flags, lighting, oversize signage — vary by state, and sometimes by county or specific route. A load that's legal to move at 12' wide in one state may need an escort at that same width one state over.

disclaimer.title: What this evaluation is, and isn't
disclaimer.body: Goliath Dispatch's oversize evaluation is operational guidance: it flags when your load's dimensions and weight are likely to require a permit or an escort, based on the state and route you provide, so your team can plan before dispatch. It is not a legal determination, and it does not replace the permit itself. Obtaining the correct permits for a load, in every state it crosses, is the operator's responsibility. When the platform's evaluation and a state's actual permit requirement disagree, the state's requirement governs — always confirm with the issuing state or your permit service before the load moves.

q1.question: Does the platform submit permit applications for me?
q1.answer: No. The platform tracks permit status, expiration and escort confirmation. It does not submit permit applications on your behalf in this release.

q2.question: What if my load is borderline?
q2.answer: Treat it as oversize. The cost of an unnecessary escort is always lower than the cost of a citation, an impound, or a bridge strike.

q3.question: Does "legal" at pickup mean legal for the whole route?
q3.answer: No. Width, height and weight thresholds change at state lines, and a multi-state route needs permits evaluated for each state individually.

q4.question: Who is responsible if a permit is wrong or missing?
q4.answer: The operator moving the load. Our evaluation is a planning tool, not a permit — see the disclaimer above.

hero.subtitle: Getting active takes one submission and a short review — not a folder of emails.

certificateOfAuthority.title: Certificate of Authority
certificateOfAuthority.body: Matched against your DOT and MC numbers with FMCSA before you're activated.

coi.title: Certificate of Insurance
coi.body: Naming the required coverage and limits, with your equipment's VIN listed on the policy.

w9.title: W-9
w9.body: A completed W-9 for tax reporting.

noticeOfAssignment.title: Notice of Assignment
noticeOfAssignment.body: Only required if you factor your invoices — it tells us to pay your factor directly, without slowing down your onboarding.

verification.title: How verification works
verification.body: Your FMCSA authority is checked against the DOT/MC you provide and re-verified automatically every 7 days for as long as you're active, not just once at signup. Your equipment's VIN is matched against your Certificate of Insurance before it can be assigned to a load, and every truck and trailer needs at least four photos before it goes active.

settlements.title: How settlements work
settlements.body: Your settlement is your gross rate plus approved reimbursable expenses, minus the dispatch fee and any approved deductions — computed the same way on every load and recorded as a permanent snapshot, so what you were paid on a load last quarter is exactly what the record still shows today.

hero.title: About Goliath Dispatch
hero.subtitle: Built by people who have run dispatch boards, not just software teams.

story.title: Why we built this
story.body: We kept seeing the same failure mode at dispatch companies: a carrier's insurance lapses, nobody notices for two weeks, and it surfaces at the worst possible moment — during a claim. Compliance gates, immutable settlements, and permits and escorts tracked next to the load itself exist because we needed them ourselves, not because they made a good pitch deck.

operationalHonesty.title: Operational honesty
operationalHonesty.body: A load that shouldn't move doesn't move. That's not a feature toggle — it's the default, with a written reason required for every override.

bilingualByDefault.title: Bilingual by default
bilingualByDefault.body: Spanish isn't a translation layer bolted onto an English product. Dispatchers, carriers and drivers who work in Spanish get the same system, not a lesser one.

auditableFinancials.title: Auditable financials
auditableFinancials.body: Every settlement is integer cents and a permanent snapshot. If a number changes, you can see exactly when, why, and by how much.

hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.counselNote: This policy is a template for operational use and should be reviewed by qualified counsel before it is relied on as your company's final legal document.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.body: This Privacy Policy describes how Goliath Dispatch ("we", "us") collects, uses, discloses and retains information in connection with the Goliath Dispatch platform, its marketing site, and related services. It applies to visitors to our marketing site, prospective and onboarded carriers, drivers, dispatch company personnel, and customers who receive a tracking link.

dataWeCollect.title: Data we collect
dataWeCollect.body: We collect information you provide directly — name, email, phone, company and DOT/MC numbers on a contact, quote or carrier-signup form; onboarding documents such as a Certificate of Insurance, Certificate of Authority, W-9 and Notice of Assignment; account and profile information once you're a registered user. We also collect information generated by using the platform — load, document and communication records, device and browser information, IP address, and, where consented, driver and vehicle location during an active load.

howWeUseData.title: How we use data
howWeUseData.body: We use data to operate the platform: evaluating carrier onboarding, verifying FMCSA authority, computing settlements and invoices, dispatching and tracking loads, evaluating oversize/permit and escort requirements, responding to inquiries, and meeting legal, tax and regulatory obligations. We do not sell personal information.

electronicSignatureConsent.title: Electronic signature consent
electronicSignatureConsent.body: Where the platform requests an electronic signature — for example, on an onboarding agreement or a rate confirmation — your action to sign electronically constitutes your consent to conduct that transaction by electronic means, and a record of the signature, including the signer, timestamp, IP address and document hash, is retained as described below.

smsConsentAndStop.title: SMS consent and STOP handling
smsConsentAndStop.body: If you opt in to receive text messages — load status updates, verification codes, or account notices — standard message and data rates may apply, and message frequency varies. You may withdraw consent at any time by replying STOP to any message, which immediately suppresses further SMS to that number; replying HELP returns support contact information. Withdrawing SMS consent does not affect email or in-app notifications.

trackingLocationDriverConsent.title: Tracking, location data and driver consent
trackingLocationDriverConsent.body: Location data is collected from a driver's device or a vehicle's tracking hardware only while a load is active, and only with the driver's or carrier's consent, recorded and revocable through account settings. Customers who receive a public tracking link see shipment status and estimated timing, not a driver's precise real-time location or personal information.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.body: Operational records — loads, documents, tracking history and related communications — are kept in the active system for 24 months, then moved to a protected archive and permanently purged no later than 5 years after archival, unless a legal hold applies. Financial records, invoices, signed agreements and signature certificates are retained for a minimum of 7 years, consistent with tax and audit requirements, and are never purged earlier than that regardless of account status. A legal hold suspends any scheduled deletion for the records it covers.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.body: We use vetted service providers to operate the platform, including hosting and database infrastructure, transactional email delivery, SMS delivery, payment processing, mapping and routing, motor carrier authority verification (FMCSA), document text extraction, and load tracking data providers. Each subprocessor is bound by a written agreement limiting its use of data to the services it provides us.

yourRights.title: Your rights
yourRights.body: Depending on your state of residence, you may have the right to request access to, correction of, deletion of, or a portable copy of your personal information, and to opt out of certain uses. Submit a request through the Contact page; we will verify your identity before acting on it and respond within the time required by applicable law. Some information cannot be deleted before its required retention period — see Data Retention above.

dataSecurity.title: Data security
dataSecurity.body: Documents and signature records are stored in private object storage with access granted only through short-lived signed URLs. Administrative access to tenant data is scoped and logged, and financial and operational records carry an append-only audit trail.

childrensPrivacy.title: Children's privacy
childrensPrivacy.body: The platform is intended for business use by adults. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18.

changesToPolicy.title: Changes to this policy
changesToPolicy.body: We will post any material change here with an updated "Last updated" date and, where required, seek renewed consent before the change applies to you.

contactUs.title: Contact us
contactUs.body: Questions about this policy or a request concerning your data can be sent through the Contact page or to the privacy contact address listed there.

acceptance.title: Acceptance of terms
acceptance.body: By accessing or using the Goliath Dispatch platform or marketing site, you agree to these Terms and Conditions and to the Privacy Policy. If you are accepting on behalf of a company, you represent that you have authority to bind that company.

description.title: Description of service
description.body: Goliath Dispatch provides software for dispatch companies to manage carrier onboarding and compliance, load dispatch, document management, invoicing and settlements, tracking, and permit and escort tracking. We are a software provider; we are not a motor carrier, freight broker, or insurer, and do not assume the regulatory obligations of any of those roles.

accountsEligibility.title: Accounts and eligibility
accountsEligibility.body: You must provide accurate registration and onboarding information and keep it current. Accounts are issued to a company and its authorized users; sharing login credentials is prohibited. We may suspend or terminate an account for a material breach of these terms, non-payment, or conduct that puts other users, drivers, or the platform's integrity at risk.

carrierResponsibilities.title: Carrier and operator responsibilities
carrierResponsibilities.body: Carriers and dispatch companies remain solely responsible for their own regulatory compliance, including maintaining valid operating authority and insurance, obtaining and carrying every permit required for a load in every state it crosses, and arranging any required escorts. The platform's oversize evaluation is operational guidance, not a legal determination — see the Heavy Haul & Oversize page. Obtaining correct permits is always the operator's responsibility, and the platform's evaluation does not shift that responsibility to us.

feesBilling.title: Fees and billing
feesBilling.body: Subscription fees, dispatch fees and any other charges are as agreed in your order form or account settings, billed on the stated cycle. Fees are non-refundable except as required by law or expressly stated otherwise.

prohibitedUses.title: Prohibited uses
prohibitedUses.body: You may not use the platform to submit false onboarding, compliance or insurance information; to circumvent a compliance gate through means other than a documented, authorized override; to interfere with the platform's security or availability; or to use another user's or carrier's data without authorization.

intellectualProperty.title: Intellectual property
intellectualProperty.body: The platform, its software, and its content are owned by Goliath Dispatch or its licensors. You retain ownership of the data you submit; you grant us the license needed to host, process and display it to operate the platform for you.

disclaimers.title: Disclaimers
disclaimers.body: The platform is provided "as is." Compliance gates, oversize evaluations and verification results are decision-support tools based on the data provided to the platform; they do not constitute legal, regulatory, insurance or permitting advice, and do not guarantee compliance with any law, regulation, or a specific state's permit or escort requirements.

limitationOfLiability.title: Limitation of liability
limitationOfLiability.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Goliath Dispatch is not liable for indirect, incidental, consequential or punitive damages, or for any citation, fine, impound, delay, or cargo loss arising from a permit, escort, or regulatory compliance failure, which remains the operator's responsibility as described above. Our aggregate liability for any claim is limited to the fees you paid us in the twelve months preceding the claim.

termination.title: Termination
termination.body: Either party may terminate as provided in your order form or, absent one, with 30 days' written notice. Financial and compliance records are retained after termination as described in the Privacy Policy's retention section.

disputeResolutionGoverningLaw.title: Dispute resolution and governing law
disputeResolutionGoverningLaw.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. Disputes will be resolved in the state or federal courts located in Tarrant County, Texas, and each party consents to that venue.

changesToTerms.title: Changes to these terms
changesToTerms.body: We will post any material change here with an updated "Last updated" date. Continued use of the platform after a change takes effect constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.
